verdict.rationale: Keycloak's first-party docs describe a built-in OAuth device authorization grant for clients that lack a suitable browser, and expose a dedicated device endpoint (/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth/device) that issues device and user codes. This directly lets CLIs and headless agents authenticate without long-lived secrets. Token revocation and introspection endpoints support managing the issued short-lived tokens. Missing for 10: detailed docs on configuring device-flow clients (polling interval, code expiry, verification URI UX), and independent or hands-on corroboration of device-flow use with CLIs or agents.
